I gather that this game has a cult following, and gods bless you guys, but Black Mirror is dull as a butter knife.  It is not a badly designed adventure game in the traditional sense -- so many adventure games suck because the designers have no idea how to create an intuitive puzzle.  That is not Black Mirror's problem.  Black Mirror's problem is just that it is boring.
I'm sure it picks up after the first four hours.  It must, because it certainly couldn't become /less/ exciting.  You realize in the opening cutscene that there's a room you will need to begin your investigation in, and four hours of fetch quests later I am still no closer to getting in that room when I first booted up the game.  I'm solving puzzles at a reasonable pace.  I'm not frustrated by the game itself.  It's the story that is putting me to sleep.
There are no small victories to celebrate, in Black Mirror.  Adventure games live or die on the feeling of progress and Black Mirror has none.  The fetch quests are just mundane tasks with no apparent relation to the mystery other than that they are things the other residents of the house require for you to earn their aid.  It all follows logically; none of it is confusing.  But why is it a 12-step fetch quest when a 3-step quest would have been more than sufficient?  It's just filler!
You learn something interesting about one NPC but he is in mourning and won't talk to you until the next day, which is apparently a scripted time jump.  You find your camera, and then film for your camera, and then you take an important picture (the one thing in my four hours that felt like progress), but you can only develop the film in town and that script hasn't triggered yet either.  You finally gain access to and earn the trust of the NPC with the key and she confides in you that she destroyed it.  The only reward for progressing in Black Mirror is more stalling.
I'm almost gleeful to to review an adventure game that is terrible for reasons other than its puzzle design, because that is so rare.  But the story of Black Mirror and its pacing still earn a thumbs down from me.  The fact that the whole thing is narrated by a breathy British emo kid zonked out on quaaludes is just the icing on the cake.

Really good story, painted background graphics that still look quite good 14 years later, solid voice acting, and some decent puzzles/mingames make this a solid game.  I played this after playing BM 2 and 3 (which are really one game split into two parts), and enjoyed having the back story filled in, and I'm looking forward to the reboot to an older time in the Gordon family saga that was recently announced.
But, man, am I glad some of the really obnoxious things adventure games like this used to do have mostly been eliminated in newer games.  There's no highlighting of items you can interact with in the environment.  I got stuck a number of times in this game, and every time it was because I missed some object in the environment, or there was something I couldn't interact with the first time I went through an area that I could later after a story trigger of some sort. You can die pretty randomly, and there is one time where you can accidentally through no fault of your own use up a required inventory item to avoid a death and have to find an older save to keep going.  Save frequently to avoid that and the other cheap deaths.  This is a long game by 2017 adventure game standards, but probably shouldn't have been so long.  There are sections that seem like pure padding.  There seemed to be really no point to having to find your way out of a mine you somehow manage to fall into for example, and if there's a door, it's got a lock that's going to require you to jump through an excessive amount of hoops to get through.  There are also several times where you ask someone to do something, they say come back later, and you have to just click around the map for 20 minutes waiting it out.
I want those 10 minutes of my life back.

Do you like to sit there for three minutes, looking at every skill on cooldown, only a hit away from death? Do you like RNG? Does RNG like you?
Get it.

That brings me to my last remark: Don't play this game to succeed, play this game to have fun exploring and expecting horrible death at every corner. Never get careless for death can hide EVERYWHERE!

Preemptive tl:dr
I recommend this game wholeheartedly to anyone who loved the first three
Dead Rising's basically my favorite series in the genre, and the fourth proves no exception. The spirit of its predecessors is strong, but the new features make gameplay flow more smoothly, which made this one more enjoyable for me than the earlier games.
Frank's as funny as ever, and it feels good to have the photography function back, especially now that it's more thoroughly integrated into gameplay for investigating. The camera's two secondary functions also provide their own unique contributions, especially using the camera to find hidden panic rooms.
There's a lot of funny little nods to previous entries in the series, and to other Capcom games too, which kept searching for newspapers, cell phones, podcasts, and zombie tags from ever getting too tedious.
The main story didn't take me too long, just shy of nineteen hours, so I'm happy I caught it on sale instead of paying full price for a relatively quick game. The replayability is strong as ever though, especially because according to the in game stats, I still have about thirty one percent of the side stuff left to do, which I'll be getting to asap because I don't feel ready to be done with Willamette yet.

Hearts of Iron IV is not your classic World War 2 Strategy game. Your not commanding your troops in battle or running around as a lone soldier in the western front. You are the leader of a country before and during the infamous war. You have many hard choices that you can make. "Should I support the allies? Should I attack Germany? Should I stay neutral?". You  can also even change your political ideology of your nation to either Democracy. (Yes you can make the Soviet Union a free capitalist country) Communist. Or Fascist(most enjoyable ideology in my personal opinion). You can also manage your military economy (although no actual money is present). And even research the nuclear bomb (Luxembourg can invent the Nuke.)
Pros: Fantastic political system
immersive gameplay that makes you feel like a leader in the 2nd World War
Many different paths you can take to lead your country to victory
Simple and interesting gameplay. (Not hard to learn)
Cons: The AI is not that smart just yet
Not enough events that does the ERA justice.
DLC is too expensive.
FINAL VERDICT
I give this game a 9/10 for its amazing and yet simple gameplay. With many paths you can take as a leader.
So what are you waiting for? Get out there and win the war! (Or conquer the world as nazis)

Before I go into the pros and cons of this game let me explicitly state that I'm reviewing this from the perspective of someone looking to see scantily clad anime chicks doing naughty things. Do not buy this with intentions of being drawn into an immersive, deep world with a complex plot. This is very much a harem/slice of life game that takes inspiration from its simplistic anime relatives. The difference being one you watch with full animation while the other you click through dialogue and watch slightly animated CG cutscenes. The result is about the same.
PROS:
- The art style is attractive enough and you get what you pay for with a game like this.
- The writing is subpar and there are typos, but the plot is still coherent and easy to follow and the girls talk dirty enough to get your jimmy a rustlin'.
- If you're not playing the hentai version, the CG scenes are still relatively raunchy and the scantily clad women abound.
- Despite what people say about the characters, each of them are pretty distinct from one another, if not fulfilling a typical stereotype for the genre.
- The soundtrack gets a bad rap, because you're having to listen to the songs on repeat as you click through dialogue. Not sure what everyone expected. On its own, it's a pretty solid compiling of music and worth a listen to.
CONS:
- I feel like the price is a little steep. Ten USD probably would have been more fair, if not lower like five USD.
- While playing, the soundtrack can get pretty repetitive. I'd suggest listening to the tracks as you move through the areas, but muting the music when in a single location for a while. The sound effects are on a separate volume option of the music, thankfully.
- The writing is subpar and there are several typos. I wouldn't mind the plot so much since, as I mentioned earlier, it's just like any other simple harem story, but the typos make me feel like they could have been more thorough with their proofreading.
Overall, I'll recommend it because there are two more "Episodes" coming which is going to be a pretty decent extra amount of action. But I HIGHLY recommend that you get the adult/hentai version from a place like MangaGamer before you buy the Steam version.

Original Review:
The game is divided in three parts and at the time of this review only part 1 is released. Part 2 and 3 are included and should be released this year.
There are a lot of visual novels coming on Steam including more and more non-japanese novels. It's hard to find quality amongst all thoses games. I personally try them all because I enjoy the experience and seeing developpers evolve and improve.
As for this one in particular, it's far from perfect, especially the spelling was pretty bad but has been patched almost the same day as release. As of the next patch the spellings and text should be fine. The script is not shakespeare's quality and the story itself is pretty basic but enjoyable. Don't buy this game thinking about getting the new Fate Stay Night or Hirugashi.
The pacing seems a bit quick but maybe they want to get the introductions over quick and the next parts will be a bit slower. You have the standard girls like clumsy, tsundere, joyful and strict so as of part 1 don't expect super special characters. They seems to have some depth to them but you only learn about it on some specific paths. Only one playthrough may leave you wondering if you skipped something.
The art is pretty clean and nice, I did not really notice the music but it is there. For now there are no voices and I think no sound effects. The engine itself is pretty good, you can pick destinations on a map while as of part one it's usually between only two choices. Don't expect a dating sims but it's a visual novels with some choices and paths.
I would like Steam to have a maybe option. I picked Yes because there are usually uncalled No reviews without any substance. You should pick it at a reduced price or at least wait until the whole game is done to see what other people think at that time. As of part 1, it's too hard to judge if the whole game will really be good or not.

Joint review for Black MIrror I, II and III:
I highly recommend finishing Black Mirror I before starting II and III.
BM I is harder, more outdated, and tends to crash if you alt-tab in the game, so save often and you may need a walkthrough. A lot of it is "hidden object" type of gaming and the objects are sometimes unfairly hidden IMHO. But something about the old style of this game makes it even more creepy, possibly more than the next two in some ways.
BM II and III were produced around the same time and are more modernized, with better graphics. They are a bit more fair and a walkthrough is not quite as necessary as with the first. The protagonist can be somewhat unlikeable if you don't like happy-go-lucky drifter kids with Boston accents. There's an option in BM II and III where you can show all clickable areas on the screen.
Overall good stories and puzzles, and a bit of a sense of humor. But mostly these are mysterious games where you are constantly looking for something, or someone. The endings of BM I and II are  very good, the ending for BM III is of course more final but also somehow less satisfying than you would expect (given we are dealing with dark magic stuff it feels pretty made-up.)

So I wanted to give an unbiased review to people who haven't played this game before, as I know the nostalgia factor is pretty big on a lot of these old AGs...myself included.  For me, this was one adventure game that slipped by me...I was aware of its existence and, even when it was on Steam it sat in my wishlist and then library for ages before I finally got around to it.
First of all, I knew that it was really old at this point and I had part of the mystery spoiled for me ages ago, but nonetheless, I was still pleasantly surprised by this little gem.
Pros:
+Beautiful settings that are richly rendered.  Yes, some of the graphics are very dated, but the settings (specifically the Black Mirror Castle) was fantastically realised and really a pleasure to explore.
+The puzzles were, for the most part, logical and fairly straight-forward to figure out.  A few were hindered by dated mechanics, but I will discuss that below.
+The story was genuinely interesting and creepy.  I think it would be a little obvious, even if the mystery hadn't been spoiled for me, but I still enjoyed watching it play out.
Cons:
-Voice acting, which most people have mentioned, is pretty appalling.  At one point I shut off the sound and just had subtitles because the main character sounded so ridiulous.
-Save often -- Approach it like an old Sierra gem and save often and KEEP MULTIPLE save files...I got myself into an unwinnable state in chapter two that I escaped only because I managed to find a saved game online...I wouldn't have replayed from the beginning otherwise.
-Mechanics -- There were a few annoying mechanics that were almost deal-breakers tbh.  Specifically, the fact that Samuel won't pick up anything that he doesn't immediately need, so there's often a LOT of backtracking.  There are also a few puzzles where you ask someone for help, then you literally just wander around until they're ready...nothing to do, just wander and go back, hoping they're ready.
-Slow as f--- -- Yeah, so there's no double-click to skip the walking animation here and a lot of the character animations and ESPECIALLY conversations are very slow.
Depsite all those cons, I DO still recommend it.  The game felt very influenced by others in the genre from the late 90s (Broken Sword and Phantasmagoria in particular, although without the dreadful FMV of the latter) that I appreciated.  So long as you approach it realising that it has many of the older pitfalls of this genre, I think you will still enjoy it...I certainly did.

I recommend it. The game is fun. It reminds me of a blend of Limbo and Trine. The puzzles aren't too hard, but there are some really good ones in there that had me stumped for a while. There are seven characters to choose from, but only three can be chosen for each run thru the game. To see the whole game, it will need to be finished at least twice. I did complete all the character-specific levels. The Scientist and the Time Traveler levels were my favorites. They were all good, though, except for possibly the level for The Monk. It was too short and too easy. It was still ok tho. There are several sections that are a part of every run-through regardless of the characters chosen. The writing is funny and the voice acting is really well done. It took about 12 or so hours to see all of the game. The art style is cartoony and pleasant. The graphics are serviceable, but nothing special. The first time dynamite blew up, the explosion crashed the game. Other than that, it ran flawlessly at a smooth 60fps throughout. My biggest gripe with the game is the amount of back tracking. There is so much back-and-worth when trying to figure out the puzzles for the first time and climbing ropes takes forever. It's not a huge deal, but its something that's ever present. Overall, The Cave was a really enjoyable experience.

What seems to start out as a simple puzzle game with influences from old classics like Maniac Mansion and the Lost Vikings actually ends up being something very unique and intriguing.
You pick three characters from a cast of seven to enter a bizarre talking cave in search of something the characters desire. You solve puzzles to progress through each area, which are closest in style to a point 'n' click. They range from very simple to relatively puzzling, but generally you can figure each one out with a few minutes of lateral thinking. If you're stuck, there's plenty of guides out there too.
The heart of this game isn't about the puzzles, however. The quirky, dark humour and the metaphor that emerges as you delve deeper drive you forward. The Cave is more than just a puzzle game, it holds a message that moves the game closer to being a piece of art.

I have to say, i dont understand these negative comments. Well, not entirely that is.
First up: Yes, you can no longer throw melee weapons and items. I miss it too guys, but honestly it's not really that bad of a thing. Instead it switches the game to having a melee, thrown/explosive and ranged weapon equipped at the same time, and you can carry whatever you like around and switch it in/out as the active weapons. Hit X and swing a weapon, turn and aim to shoot one in the face, hit X again to swing and run away and drop a grenade or whatever you currently had equiped in the thrown slot. It makes it very action oriented. The old system was a little lacking sometimes due to having to switch, so it's an improvement all the same despite you missing out on some humor that throwing a pie in someone's face gave instead of eating it.
Second: Yes, the time limit is gone. Some like it, some dont. I actually like it. They put a LOT of work in details, and this lets you explore all you want and see every sight, gimmick and secret if you can put in the time to find it. And there are hundreds of them. Yes, it's not really the old Dead Rising feel of be at X-location at Y-time for a specific event to trigger, and having to replay the game a hundred times over to discover them all. But it was also stressful. Many of you are upset it's gone, but you guys probably dont remember how anoying it was at times when you were trying to get somewhere, stopped to have a look at something you never saw before, and ran out of time or missed an event. Not to mention the required events that you werent allowed to miss and had to be at, or your game was over. This is a lot better, and they still have semi-random events and triggered events by certain actions.
That all said and done. The game is massive, beautiful, interesting and there's a ton of detail poured into it. Some of the weapons are a little over the top, but that's honestly the only thing i dont fully endorse. They are fun though. There is so much to do and see. There is something relaxing about taking on the zombie apocalypse with swords, guns and what not.
And lets not forget, if you should ever feel done with the regular game, there actually is proper MULTIPLAYER now. Really fun concept, and you can level seperately from your main game for every of the characters you choose. It's kind of a competitive co-op game. It's best if you all survive, but there is a point count at the end, you can choose not to let everyone reach the safe room and abandon people if you feel you can make it by yourself. It also brings back timers since if you're not at the safe room by 0:00 on the countdown you dont survive the night. It's really rough for as far as i've tried it, you really need to work together.

I want to say this game is good.  Though I have to be honest I dont know if it is.  A while back i was invited to test this game....and didnt due to lack of time.  It came out so now i decided to give it a try.  The first thing i noticed is that this game is on a free to play model now with a subscription if you want one.  Thats neat...and i suppose some people hate it or like it.  Anywise I downloaded the game and was immediately given the ability to log into the game with an account or as a guest.  I decided to reclaim my old account to do this.  Anywise....i started up the game and was immediately told about a patch and how i could play but had to wait for downloading in game...since the big patch was big.
So i went into the game....and decided to make a character.  A few deceptions became evident.  First off 6 races....there is only 3 per side....you have to choose a side...with each race simply being an analog of the others...with slight changes to looks and some slight different abilities they can get.  Already with this mechanic i can see this game is going to be full of issues and other weirdness.
You dont make a game requiring you to play sides...sorry thats an automatic going to make the game lame function.....but maybe i can slog through anywise.
So i made a character.....noticed the graphics for some of my choices had not loaded yet.....ok warning sign two.....the red flags with this issue are evident....those pictures should have been loaded a while back but where not....means bad optimization and probably bad other things......if they are too lazy to fix something like that which is a simple fix...then they are probably too lazy for much story or fun gameplay.....ok goign to try to slog through that as well.
So i start the game and get a...failed to connect to server and black screen,
Been like this for over 15 minutes.......i have a black screen with what i assume is a waiting load icon.
At this point with these issues like this......i can say maybe this game is fun....but these red flags show....a huge amount of issues.....if they have this sort of thing happening.....the game is probably fairly bad.
but i am going to slog through or try too.....
even though this rating says recommend.....i may alter it.....if i can ever play this game.
Ok I finaly got into the game....graphicwise it isnt bad...both sides start with similar quests.
Flow of the game is typical.....but i can see this is definately is a cash shop game....lots of things locked requiring unlocks and a plethora of things to buy in the cash shop.  Control wise its typical has a power bar....which you can flip pages on and you can add power bars which is a huge plus.
Only draw back for powers is this game uses the archaic and idiot global cool downs.  As in you use one attack and 5 of your other attacks are cooling down....in the real world someone isnt going to stand around waiting so many seconds to use a differing manuever....unrealistic....and annoying.
But onthe plus side you can have many powers and use many power bars.
You can change your focus of abilities as well...as long as you have not spent souls on powers in a focus....and unfortunatly some of the focus' seam to duplicate each other....only the names and some graphics are different for skills.
So the supposed many focus things is a bogus lie....but then it does add to the concept of tailor making your character.
I find myself disapointed with this game....with those features in those ways....but i will slog through to see what the rest of the game offers.
Ok so following the main storyline...we find we get cutscenes....and a very disjointed storyline.  Storyline is the world you are on has these rifts to other worlds opening and wreaking havoc....possibly this is due to a war with gods.
Each faction side player is a resurrected hero....one side represents some holy divine group .while the other group wants to protect it a different way.  Looking at costumes and things I believe its a matter of one uses technology while the other uses magic.....storywise its not very clear why they are against each other or what the division truly is....as you can see on the side that supposedly uses magic...totems and things are actualy constructs from technology items.
At a certain point you fight bad guys who you get told have come from rifts....but for whatever reason at a ceratin point you get sent back in time...to prevent the war and fix the world....not sure why this is done....because the point you get sent too...is just as hosed as the place in time you left....go figure on the logic.
Anywise while running around you will get the usual quests and missions...and also run into rifts that open giving further mini-quests.

This is an old game now. One that I never got around to play when it first came out. I was eager to see what I had missed. After completing it I sit with somewhat mixed emotions about the whole experience, and here's why:
The game is old so don't expect high resolution graphics or smooth animations. I'm sure this was on par with the time it came out and in no way does it ruin the experience much playing it today. Everything seems to be moving a bit slowly though.
The story itself is intriguing and interesting and left me wanting to figure out what happened and how and was one of the main reasons I stayed in it to the end. Unfortunately at the conclusion I felt quite disappointed. A lot of mystery built up around the events in the game was left unanswered and it also felt quite anticlimactic.
I felt the characters in the game could have been fleshed out more and made more interesting but you can tell they at least tried. Voice overs ranged from good to bad. While some had emotion and charm, others had as much charisma as an empty pack of cigarettes. And most dialogue was slow and tedious.
And there is a lot of dialogue in this game, so if you don't like that you are in trouble. I don't mind a lot of dialogue if it tells a good story and keeps being interesting, but here I felt several times it could have been shortened or made a bit more exciting. The worst parts were probably the voiced written notes/books you find from time to time. Some of them took forever. Luckily you can read them faster and skip through the dialogue.
What buggers me the most about this game is some of the game design decisions. For the first time, that I can remember, I managed to save my game in the absolutely worst place possible and was unable to continue playing the game, unless I would do a whole lot over again. And it is far from obvious that it would be a fatal place to save. The frustration was noticable seeing I had invested about 7 hours in the game at the time. Fortunately I could find a save online at that very spot and was able to finish the game. So yes, in this game you can actually die, so remember to save often, and use several saves. I'll share the details (as spoilerfree as possible) at the end of the review for the ones who wants to be forewarned.
The other extremely frustrating game design choises are several instances where you need to get help from one of the characters and they need time to complete the task for you. This leaves you to wander around aimlessly as there is no way to progress any other part of the story until that task is completed. And sometimes it takes forever. You can be wandering from scene to scene for a good long time, come back to the character, only to be told he/she isn't done yet and you have to continue wandering around. What the hell were they thinking? Does anybody EVER like to be left with nothing to do when they play a computer game? The worst part is that this happens several times. Also, you can be pixelhunting in a screen, not being able to pick anything up, only to be sent back later to pick up these exact same objects. Not only that, but you have to go back to screens picking up items that wasn't even marked when you were there the first time. Try to make a note of what you can see in the various screens so you will have a bit easier way of finding them when you are tasked with that. Some items are also very hard to spot whether they are active or not and that will certainly cause some hunting through several large areas.
Several puzzles in this game are the same sort of puzzles you expect to find in a Hidden Object game (not cluttered screens though) and feel a bit cheap. I enjoy puzzles like that but expect a bit more from "real" adventure games.
I did experience a few bugs too, but not to much of a problem. The pointer disappeared a couple of times and could only be fixed by closing the game in the task manager and loading the last save. Alt-TAB may cause the game to crash.
Overall I can't really recommend this game. It is slow, riddled with horrible game design choices and quite frankly it is a bit old. If you are a true adventure fanatic you might enjoy it, but there are so many games that are way better than this.

Having played several hours of this on a DRM Free version, and a few here on steam as well, I can honestly say this about the game:
It is not worth your money unless it is at a steep, steep discount. The premise showed a lot of promise, and the early Alpha showed a game that would be very addicting and fun once it was polished, added to and developed further. There were spelling errors, very barebones gameplay and little to no explanation for the things you did, along with no options for graphics or sound. But it was fun, and it was Alpha.
Now the game is released and.... not much has changed honestly. A lot more has been added to it, but very few of its glaring problems have been worked on or fixed. The game seems to assume you have a base knowledge of at least the game types that are being simulated, and if you don't it is not going to do anything to explain what is happening or why. Graphic and sound options are spartan, actually playing the game feels almost as much of a grind as the actual games themselves.
Spelling errors still abound, and despite the apparent polish of the game it is clear that not much resources were poured into, or on hand for this game. A lot of great concepts are left half finished ,and a lot of promised features just simply never were added in.
This game is a collection of great ideas that never really went anywhere. I'm severely disappointed that the promise I saw in Alpha and paid money to support was takne nowhere.

I have played Evolve previously, back during a free weekend and there have been a fair amount of changes, some good, some bad.
The good:
1. The new 4 ability for the trapper is very useful, giving you a general direction of where the monster is, and boosting the trapper's speed temporarily. The switch in the support's 4 ability from a cloak to a shield is excellent, saving a wounded team in a pinch in many situations.
2. The ability for each hunter to call the dome down is extremely useful, compensating for trappers that are lagging behind the team, and also giving the team more encouragement to spread out to pin the monster down.
3. The increase in monster abilities from the start of the game allows them to access all of their abilities at the beginning if they wish it, or increase damage and cooldown to the powers they prefer early.
The bad:
1. The matchmaking system has not been stabilized yet, often causing parties to repeatedly exit and reenter the queue because 1 or more members got kicked out with the notification "The Lobby is Full".
2. The hunters have no knowledge of what monster the enemy picks before they have made their selections, possibly dooming a hunter team to be at a serious disadvantage if they have selected hunters that the monster is good at disrupting.
3. In the free weekend I played a long time ago, the biggest concern when playing a match was facing a Wraith. The rest of the monsters I had faced were tough, depending on the player, but felt balanced and overall fun to fight against. The Wraith instantly brought down the hunting teams morale and many of them would audibly groan on the mic, or disconnect entirely. I have found the the "nerfs" the have been implemented to balance the Wraith have never truly made it an enjoyable match, and the same pattern continues to this day. I have fought as and fought against the Wraith, but found that the Wraith has too many benefits to make it a feasible character for public matches. The mobility of his dashes, being able to ascend like the kraken, and use his first ability as a dash made avoiding even a team that had a skilled trapper child's play. I have fought Gorgons, Goliaths, Krakens, Behemoths, and each of their variations, but found that each had a major flaw that could be exploited, except for the Wraith. I dislike that this particular section of this review is so long, but it is frustrating to me to see an imbalance that the developers have created and avoid making any significant effort to avoid the frequent 10, 20, and 30 win streaks I have seen on several occasions facing someone who constantly picks Wraith.
Overall, I love the new changes to the game and think its potential is amazing, but there are things the developers should go back and evaluate before they take the next steps.

A mix between Ark: survival evolved, subnautica, rust and space engineers. This game has it all! It is challenging while also being fair. To make this review easier for me to make I'm going to section it like so:
.Resource gathering
.Fighting
.Exploration
.Building
.TL:DR at the bottom
Lets begin...
Resource gathering
Resource gathing in this game is a mix of ARK and space engineers, where you use your pick to gather resources and you get them automatically and can chose to pick up the chunks of rock that brak as well. Your pick itself doesn't break but the challenge of mining in this is to make sure your safe and don't become over-encumbered otherwise your food for any predator roaming by. THe system itself is complex but not too hard to grasp, where you need certain items to gather certain thing when you start to get into the more complex stuff (such as having to make certain conatiners for gases) which makes the gathering system feel unique.
Fighting
The fighting in this is nice and balanced, you have to time your dodges to avoid being stunned by enbemies and their various lunges and projectiles (not to mention the giant worm that jumps at you when you go near a sand dune!). You have a assault rifle with limited ammo and a pistol with infinite ammo but it has a short cool down before you can fire again. It makes you feel powerful but not over powered.
Exploration
This game is BIG and the world has a lot for you to discover, and your overall speed is affected on what your currently holding I.e. if you have your assault rifle out you run slower than if you were to have nothing or you pick in hand. This means if you are over-encumbered and are trying to return home you need to make sure your not holding stuff so you go at your maximum speed. Also like space engineers you can explore space, making it another rare survival game in space (but don't explect to be launching rockets from the get-go!).
Building
This is when the ultimate mix happens, the game is like rust in the sense that you can add indoor items like chemistry tables and forges along with the ability to choose what wall goes on each section of your habitat module (although there isn't varying tiers such as stone to metal, but you can change the wall type like windows and such). The subnautica aspect comes into play since you can't choose what you building looks like as it comes as a pre-made model that you piece together with other modules, but the building require a lot of pieces like a jigsaw puzzle, so the finished thing looks and works well.
Overall this game has a lot of potential and as it is the features are nice and the visuals are superb. Definitelly an early access worth getting (or in the very least keeping an eye on).
EDIT: I also forgot to mention that the game also relates to ARK by allowing you tu upgrade your character and chose what you want to spec into to improve you ability to survive, so there another handy lil' feature.
TL:DR Keep an eye on this game at the very least, it has nice visuals and challenging mobs to combat, along with a detailed gathing and creating system. Also has a nice feeling build system that is very satisfying.

The Cave allows you to play as three of seven unique characters, each with their own mannerisms and animations. As you descend the depths of The Cave, you'll have to utilize their abilities to conquer whatever bizarre challenge lies in the way leading up to their own personal section of The Cave where your "hero" is perfectly willing to show how far he/she is willing to go to obtain his/her goals.
A typical playthrough will take about 3 or 4 hours, even if you don't know what you're doing. There's a lot of backtracking and out-of-the-box thinking, akin to Adventure games, and there are some platforming segments but they're hardly difficult since dying doesn't change a thing. If you don't mind the backtracking, wait until your second or third playthrough (since there are seven characters and you can only take three at a time. You'd be crazy not to experience the story of every character). It didn't bother me at all and - let's face it - a lot of games these days have backtracking, even on a larger scale than this. Only the third playthrough will tire on you unless you pick your two favorite characters to accompany the last guy since four sections of The Cave will always remain the same no matter which characters you pick.
The game really isn't difficult or mentally taxing but it isn't very long either, which can be a good thing. So I recommend this game to anyone, just as long as the repetion and lack of action doesn't throttle you and you can stomach doing something evil. But understand that there are SOME refunds in The Cave. At least the one that matters.

It's what everyone says about it - a beautiful game with great art inspired by 30s cartoons.
Everyone keeps saying it's hard, but nobody ever quite explains why. I'd like to try to.
The game isn't like most platformers or run-and-gun games. Those usually use 2 buttons- shoot and jump. If there are other moves in the game like dashes or super attacks, they are assigned secondary inputs, like one of the buttons plus a directional, or holding down one of the buttons- for example, most platformers with dash moves let the user input them by double-tapping the horizontal input for the desired direction. However, Cuphead insists on a separate button for dashing.
The game also features super moves, which are assigned to ANOTHER button. This makes for a clunky control experience- one that often had me getting confused- it wasn't quite intuitive to me. If you want to dash, surely you press the walk buttons quickly, right? And this sounds like a small issue- Cuphead has configurable controls, right? But they don't allow for the remapping of controls to multiple inputs, or more complex inputs like double taps.
The control remapping is an issue for another reason - the controller support is clunky at best- a real issue for a hardcore platform/run-and-gun game where tight and easy controls are expected. You can either play with the keyboard, where the controls are awkwardly stretched along a wide section of the keyboard (which I found made them quite confusing) or you can play with a controller- which is a pain to map to your preferred keys, and doesn't work in any menus!
You can tell me to git gud, but I can't git gud when I can't connect my controller properly and even when I do I can't set the controls to what I'm used to.

This game is actually one of my favourites ever, I absolutely love the gameplay, storyline, and characters.
Gameplay
It's a fast paced side scroller that is all about hype. Once you get your Kudos to 1000 the music and screen changes and it's worth it to keep is there, despite how hard it may be sometimes. The tagging and shocking enemies may seem a little tedious at the beginning but it gets to be more fun later on. There are a good share of secrets (hidden characters and gems) that can be pretty damn hard to get sometimes (I'M LOOKING AT YOU, GEM IN THE FRICKIN BIOCHEM PLANT) and unlockables such as new guns and abilities for you to try out and have fun with, so if you want to get everything it'll take a minimum of 25 hours or so.
Story/Characters
Ehhhh... The story isn't amazing, but it's pretty good. Although the CHARACTERS have a lot put into them. I'm not just talking about the conversations between Joule and Gunvolt, although those are the characters with the most story and personality. They put a lot of work into the conversations during the missions if you decide to do the japanese voices with english subs, and if you really want to look into their backstories, Inti Creates has a short story of each of their backstories online.
Okay, maybe the port isn't the greatest (this was originally a 3DS game) but if you grab a good controller and some headphones this game can be a great experience.
Oh yeah, and AZURE STRIKER GUNVOLT 2 HYPE!!!

Good for those looking for a solid platformer, but even better for score-hunters and challenge gamers.
Azure Striker Gunvolt can be divided into two separate games. The first one is that everyone will experience for the first playthought. During around 5-6 hours of gameplay you will be enjoying yourself with interesting twist on the Megaman formula (replacing classic jump'n'shooting with tagging'n'zapping), great pixel art, decent but not amazing soundtrack and the plot which is definately something stupid. Story is like a distilled definition of every anime cliché you can think of and it's so unapologetic that it's entertaining on its own way. Don't expect a good plot, but if you find some amusement in boss characters (that are really ninely designed and programmed BTW) yelling their desperation attacks in broken engrish with colorful splash screens for punctuation, then you will be satisfied.
I really need to praise the gameplay. It's interesting and fun enough for the "mortal" fan of platformers with quite reasonable difficulty. Game handles the challenge in a clever way - giving you helpful equitable, "training wheels" items by default, that make normally Megaman-level hard game more inviting to newbies. You can always turn them off and equip something else if you find those too insulting to your pride.
After you run out of story content, the second "game" starts - hunting for S+ ranks. It's a challenge where many, previously unimportant and ignored mechanics, like crafting, skills and equipment come to play and if you like a hard as nails tasks, then look no further. Getting high scores requires fast clear times, spotless dodging skills and understanding of pretty clever scoring mechanics. It's immensely rewarding feeling, when after several hours you finally nail "that" stunt.
If you don't like a challenge and you are looking just for classic action platformer with beginning and end, the price can be a bit steep for you. While it is a solid title, it doesn't take too long to beat. A moderate price drop should suffice in this case. However, if you like learning boss patterns, memorizing levels and doing ballet between bullets on the highest levels multiple times then you can take Azure Striker from the get go. It will be painful and you will love it.
One more thing, I forgot to mention. This game doesn't have the best port in the universe. Be prepared to sit a bit in the options menu to set up your gamepad correctly and to endure 30FPS lock. Those issues aren't dealbreakers, but be vary of those.

On it's own, Dead Rising 4 is a somewhat enjoyable experience, however, within the franchise of Dead Rising, it stands as a poor example of game development. In the franchise, it feels rushed and created with a lack of love and care, with it's dismissal of many fan-favouite mechanics, such as: The Timer, weapon throwing, Picking up (almost) everything and using it as a weapon, a mall with expansive stores and other areas, and great characters and story. multiple endings. For an example: I am a major fan of two other Series' besides Dead Rising, those being Saints Row and Metal Gear Solid. This game does to the Dead Rising what Saints Row IV (and to a lesser extend, The Third) and Metal Gear Solid V did to their respective franchises. They are fun to play, however, within their franchises they are poor games, mostly lacking in the area of story. This leads me onto my next point, the story of Dead Rising 4. The story is lacking in all departments, the characters are underdeveloped horribly, and that is the least of it. Dead Rising 4's story is just horribly lacking, and seems to throw out the very indepth writing of the 2006 Classic. Frank shouldn't have returned, nor Willamette because neither are even remotley the same. Frank's personality is completley different, becoming a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This could have starred anyone who's name ends a 'K' and could have been set anywhere. There was no reason to bring either back, because the devs didn't bring the series back to it's roots, they simply baited old fans to come back due to nostalgia amongst other things. Not to mention the voice actor change, which they said was to make Frank more mature (despite him being even less mature than before), but was more likely the fact that TJ Rotolo was on strike at the time, and the game had to be developed for Christmas of 2016. And I have no idea as to why they're hiding Franks new voice actor (His name is Ty Olsson, I believe). Anyway, I can't even begin to explain the story, because honestly? I haven't completed it. Why? Because I haven't bought the Frank Rising DLC. It's very much common knowledge that the ending of Dead Rising 4 isn't in the game, and this shows the worst side of game development. The game is lazy, and should not stand under the title of Dead Rising. Capcom, despite all the game's screwups, have a solid foundation for a game with Dead Rising 4, though, it is just that: A foundation. It's horribly underdeveloped, and after playing on both Xbox One and PC, I can say the PC version is inferior to the XBONE version (though both versions are buggy), whilst not a horrible port on the level of Arkham Knight or Saints Row 2, it's not at all great.
TL;DR
Dead Rising 4 is fun, but is a horrible game within it's franchise. Buy it if you don't care about the story, and/or just want to have fun killing zombies without any rush or difficulty.
Capcom, please make Dead Rising 5 vastly improve on the mess that was 4. Bring back Rotolo if possible, and if you are bringing characters of old back? Do not make them different people with the same name. Do not make the ending DLC, Do not give us a game that can be flown through with ease, give us a challenge. Bring back the timer. Give us a better story, characters and multiple endings. And for the love of God, give us a better PC Port.
Edit: I wouldn't reccomend buying the game at full price (Currently £39.99). I'd wait until it's discounted a bit.
Edit 2: To add on to my requests for Capcom for DR5, I'd also like to see Co-Op return. Along with a better lot of Combo weapons.

Ok, I've just finished The Cave, which took me around 4 hours in total. It's... alright. Not great, not bad, just alright.
You have a choice of three from seven characters to choose from for your adventure. I took the Knight, the Hillbilly, and the Adventurer. Each playthrough starts the same way and ends the same way, but you have three small "story" sections bespoke to each character, which makes specific use of that character's special ability (the Knight has a shield ability, for example). The story sections are amusing enough and some of the puzzles got me stuck for a while, but overall it just feels a bit... undercooked. It's like it could've been just something a bit more.
The style is cool, it's reasonably funny in places, it's just not as good as I wanted it to be. Maybe I've misjudged it and I'm not their target audience, it does have a certain charm to it, I just felt like I was playing through it to complete it rather than to see what the story did.
Unless you're absolutely dying to play it - in which case you've probably already bought it - I'd really wait for a 50-75% off sale (probably the latter).
TL: DR; there's better Double Fine games available. It's not bad, just not as good as it could've been.

Well I had high expectations for this one. Its meets many of those expectations without any doubts. Wonderful visuals without having to drift backwards in graphics quality.  Seems many old school adventure game developers feel that in order to get that old school feel the graphics need to suffer. In this case it proves you can have both classic gaming wrapped in charming graphics.  Very interesting twist having 7 characters to choose from, each with their own unique skills or special abilities.
This goes along with a lot of the more recent adventure style games requiring multiple characters. One needs to be sent to hold a certain lever, another to pull on something else while the 3rd is there to accomplish the task. Each of 7 characters has a special gift or ability. The adventurer had her lasso in order to swing from over head features while the "Twins" can leave phantoms of themselves in place. Overall a great title, certainly does not disappoint. Puzzles are hard to enough to keep me interested. Very little if NO hand holding with this one. One thing the screenshots dont do justice to just how charming and nice the graphics are. Very well done title.

I was considering buying this game when it first came out, but I was a little reluctant (it just looked like a free to play game to me) and I put it off. Then for some time I forgot about it.
Now I saw it became free to play a few days ago, and I can say I'm pretty happy with it. It's a no-nonsense kind of game that doesn't really pull any micro-transaction ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t on you. But in saying that I realise that I wouldn't mind if they had something I could pay for. Now that I've got a feel for the game I can say I really like it, and of course I want to support the Devs, so I wouldn't mind if there was a little bit of micros in there.
If they added micro-transactions I'd only want them to be something where you buy keys with real money, and then can unlock skins or characters with them, nothing that changes the gameplay in any significant form.
Now onto the game, it is extremely fun, but only if everyone is good at it. When you get stuck on a team with someone who is unfamiliar with the mechanics or what each class is used for, it can get pretty stressful. For any new players I really reccommend playing the tutorials first, 1) because they actually help you progress in rank, 2) so you know what to do in fast thinking situations when your friends need you. I've been in far too many situations where a medic will do nothing but try to play as an attacker the whole time, and our team almost dies out instantly.
But when you get a good squad going, you can beat even the most OP monsters. That is of course if you don't encounter a player who only plays monster and every time just runs away until he's level 3, then messes you all up. So really I have no complaints about this game as of yet, especially since it's FREE. :D
Will update if something comes up though.

Basically, if left clicks are getting you nowhere, try a right click on things you can interact with until it does something.

Save often. There are a few places you may regret it if you don't do so. Additionally, a few times, the game glitched on me and I had to quit out. Had I not been saving regularly, that would have caused a fair amount of frustration.

A good point-and-click game, despite its flaws.
I would only recommend Black Mirror to fans of the genre. It's generic and sometimes frustrating, but then again, so are most of these games. Though more of a mystery than a horror story, lovers of the macabre may consider their needs served in this game.
The graphics are a mixed bag: the animations really show their age and are clunky and sluggish, but the beautiful backgrounds more than make up for this. Sound is alright, though I found the voice-acting to be a bit bland (note: I played the game with Russian audio).
The puzzles are also two-sided. A lot offer just the right amount of challenge, but others were a drag. There were many times where I just stopped bothering, checked a walkthrough, and then rolled my eyes about how unsatisfying the solution was. There's also some "pixel hunting" involved (essential items being very hard to spot on screen), and a damnable hard 'slider puzzle' (you've seen it before: a scrambled board of 4x4 moveable squares, with one open spot) halfway in the game.
Rather unforgivable though, is a set-up at about two thirds in the game, where you have a gun with two bullets and need to get passed a shut gate. If you do not properly inspect the lock first, the protagonist will miss the first shot, and if you save at this point (as I did...) you are royally screwed when you come face-to-face with an angry wolf mere moments later.
Another gripe I have is that the game sometimes stops it own pace by having you consult another character for advice, only to be told that he or she needs some time for research. What happens then is that you'll spend five or ten minutes just aimlessly walking around until the character finally decides to share their vital piece of information with you.
Despite all this nitpicking, I'd still say it's not a bad game by any means. But like I said: it's only recommend for the seasoned point-and-click lovers. Buy it on sale and it'll probably be worth it.

I was starting to like this game. The point and click aspects are generally logical, the story is intriguing, and it has pretty good backgrounds and characterisation. After 4 hours of gameplay some things really started to niggle.
The first is a biggy if you ask me - that the solution to a number of problems is to wait for an indeterminate amount of time for a solution - either an object or an answer you need. There is literally nothing to do in this time other than walk around, looking at the same things you have already investigated and feeling horrendously bored. If there was something else you could do i.e. mini games or similar then this would be ok, but it feels very much like the game is just fleshing out the time taken. I'm sure there were plenty of other games out there at the time this was made that did this, but it's still lazy. It would make far more sense if you had to complete a task before you could get the answer.
The second is some of the puzzles. There are no clues about the solution. Now this can be great if it involves lateral thinking or logic, but this makes for some very frustrating game play as you're left randomly trying combinations to see what actually works. Again, it could be that I've now lost patience with something that was common at the time, but I find it infuriating.
The third is that it would be better with a few more prompts from your character. Thankfully if there's still something to be done in an area he refuses to leave, but the help he gives is far more sporadic after that. It would be helpful, for example, if he gave some logical hint as to why he doesn't want to do something, thus prompting you to look for another solution.
Perhaps I am being overly harsh on a very old game, but this has now got to the point where I have stopped enjoying it. Sure that, all in all, if you can get past these niggles that it's still enjoyable and I know it has quite a following, but still I'm fast losing patience.

After playing RIFT for several months I have to say i do really enjoy the game. I have not yet experienced Raids which i hope to do soon, but the leveling was pretty fast but fun with many quests and random "Rifts" to encounter along the way for extra exp. The instant Adventures are an instant raid group for random quests in a chain for great Exp and quick groups, that's not to mention the dungeon finder for random or specific.
And the best part has to be the "REX" This allows you to pay to get 1250 credits on the store (enough for 15 days of Patron or membership) from other players for a set price (As of March 4, 2014 That price is 900Plat in game) Essentially allowing you to pay for membership or items with in game currency rather then money. Now by the time you hit 60 you should have close if not enough for a REX and you can begin to use the Auction House to sell your items to attain another and so on. You may also buy a REX and sell it for in game currency or gift it to a friend (Or random if you are really nice )
All in all I would Recommend RIFT to anyone looking for a fun MMO that constantly delivers in Pve, Pvp and tradeskills. If you don't have a lot of time like me, or don't have money like me the REX is great to take advantage of those EXP boosts or those recipes you've wanted for awhile or just want a Patron pass for bonus exp and loot. The choice is yours in RIFT.

My review of this game is not exactly a negative one. I still enjoy this game but there're a few problems.
I encountered 2 game-breaking errors during 3-hour gameplay. First one was pretty bad and I had to relog my PC. I tried the classic Alt+F4 trick before I relogged but it didn't work. And somehow a Windows update reset my task manager's settings to default and the task manager was no longer set to "Always On Top" so I couldn't force shut down the game process. Second error made the game crash. I don't know why but, I pressed Enter to skip a cutscene in Act 2 and the game just crashed.
Singleplayer compaign is not open-world because you don't have an open world to move around. It's a narrative singleplayer experience which focuses on story-telling, like Crysis series.
The game gets repetitive really fast because for 90% of the time you have to kill enemies with your sniper rifle. Pistol is almost useless unless you're in a tight situation when you are surrounded by alarmed enemies in close proximity. Melee kill has not much chance to shine as well.
The Digital Extra DLC has some sort of bugs or it's even unavailable. I had the DLC but I could not find it in game. There was no such a button called "Downloadable Contents" on the main menu until I bought the other 2 DLCs - World Hunter Pack and Siberian Strike.
No one really plays multiplayer of this game now. So if you're going to buy the game, just get the base game and the Siberian Strike DLC. The other 2 DLCs are for multiplayer.
Edit 1 (Q&A):
1. Is the game still worth the full price today?
- No. Because based on what I can see, multiplayer is a big part in this game. If you cannot enjoy every part of the game then do not pay full price.
2. How much discount do you recommend?
- At least 33.3% off I'd say.
3. How do you think about the Siberian Strike DLC? Is is worth it?
- I haven't progressed that far into the game. I will update my review once I finish everything in the singleplayer compaign.

If you want a relatively easy entry into the world of roguelikes, ToME is definitely the game for you. While you don't need to learn a billion different key combinations in order to do the actions you want, you will most likely be overwhelmed by the massive amounts of activateable skills and items that you earn over the game. The character building options will also most likely overwhelm you. Your characters will be trash for a while until you get the hang of the system.
Having the option to play on modes that aren't quite as punishing as roguelike is always a plus for those getting into roguelikes, but where's the fun in that? I mean, I did just play a single character for some twenty odd hours before dying on the last boss, losing all the progress. I wasn't mad. Honest.
For whatever it's worth, ToME is the first game in closer to half a decade that has caused me to play for seven hours in a row. Seven. Hours.
Get it. Reward the active developers of the game. Or don't. I'm not your dad.

Hello, this is my first serious review.
I'm an avid gamer and dedicate most of my free time to gaming and checking out titles that could be cool and fun.
Pro Gamer Manager did have an appeal at the start... same Game Dev Tycoon art... managing your own eSports team... so I figured the mechanics would be similar, thus, making it a fun and entertaining experience. I was wrong.
I can see the devs tried to make an entertaining title, but the formula does not work. In MANAGING GAMES you want to see that the decisions and actions you take, affect the outcome of the matches whether in a good or bad way. But when you play Pro Gamer Manager, the decisions you make, affect the outcomes in a really vague way or they don't affect it in any way and are unable to change its outcome.

You never know or are told (at least give us a hint of how the mechanics work for god's sake) how things are going to affect your results. You can pickup styles and different tactics but they are really vague on how you should use them and really basic. They try to make it simple but making it that way just takes away the whole experience of being a Professional eSports team.
Even if the devs assume you're used and knowledged about MOBA or FPS games, it's difficult to figure out what to do in every situation, even with Trial and Error. I might be wrong if I say that the decisions you take as a manager or a player DO NOT affect the outcome BUT; when I played Pro Gamer Manager I always felt that way and, believe me, IT IS NOT A PLEASANT FEELING.
I really tried to find something redeeming and have fun with Pro Gamer Manager, but either I haven't tried hard enough (prob not) or the game in itself isn't fun, probably the latter.
It also has some bugs that are not gamebreaking or really important, but they are really simple and basic bugs that kind of break the experience too (16-15 as a valid victory result on a FPS match even if it's not meant to be CS, can't click too fast on incoming messages or they will delete themselves).
Pro Gamer Manager defeats its own purpose as a game and a managing game, such potential wasted because of a bad execution.
I wouldn't recommend to buy this game in its current state, it's basically not fun for me and I've requested a refund.

Cuphead's fluid, 1930s-style hand-drawn animation will probably be the first thing that sticks out to the casual observer, but it's not just a pretty face: Anyone who's cut their teeth on the likes of Gunstar Heroes and Contra will find a lot to love about this game, as the challenge ramps up further and further with each passing level. Unlike those games, however, Cuphead has a higher ratio of boss battles to platforming levels, and each of them are unique and well-designed from both an aesthetic and technical standpoint. Be prepared to try, try, try again, as the game is punishingly difficult, something that may be off-putting to the average gamer; still, Cuphead is at no time unfair, and it gives the player unlimited lives. All of this is accompanied by a jazzy soundtrack that perfectly captures this era of animation. Two-player co-op is also available at any time, but the action can get a bit chaotic with two players on the screen. Cuphead is one of those rare titles that reminds me why I started playing games in the first place.

DEAD RISING 4
PUBLISHER – CAPCOM
DEVELOPER – CAPCOM Game Studio Vancouver
GENRE – Horror/Comedy/Action
THE BASICS:
You've played this game before – for better for worse. Zombies are about, and somebody's gotta waste 'em. Might as well be you.  Looks like it's time to slap a couple grenades onto a sledgehammer and go to town. Our intrepid reporter sets off to get his story, and document it all with his trusty camera. New options include new camera modes (nightvision and a deus-ex-machina hacker-type mode/spectral analyzer), as well as new blueprints for slapping two weapons together (e.g. a sledgehammer and some grenades), or even two vehicles, to make something quite nicer than the sum of its parts. All weapons and vehicles do have a limited durability, though, so choose carefully. You have a fairly deep skill tree to invest in as you go and level up; put your first few points into the one that gives you bonus health and regeneration; you won't regret it.
THE FLOW AND THE STORY:
Frank West's path has brought him right back to everyone's favorite zombie-infested mall, years after the initial outbreak, in a time where (supposedly) everyone has already been inoculated with the vaccine. And yet, there are plenty of undead hordes to be found. Oopsie.
CONTROLS:
Standard and controller; supports XBONE controller out of the box. Movement and in-game camera/view controls are simple and straightforward, as are the melee weapon controls – one button for normal attack, tap another for a “clear out attack”/hold for a powerful slam, both together once your hit counter is high enough for a satisfyingly gruesome finishing move. Shoulder button tap to throw, or hold for precise placement. Ranged weapons are a bit finicky, but usable. D-pad to select weapon types, repeated click to cycle among available weapons in the same category. Driving controls can take some getting used to (shoulder buttons for fwd/back, stick for some rather loose steering (those go-karts handle like cows), triggers for weapons).
GRAPHICS:
Dark. What, you were expecting bright and cheerful? Neon lights and the occasional fire light up some areas, while others either have little to no lighting to help you on your way. Fortunately. You can still move around while in camera mode/nightvision/spectral analyzer in order to compensate.
SOUND:

This is a solid P&C adventure game. It definitely has some rough edges, but the good bits more than make up for it.
The rough edges mainly involve miscalculations (in my opinion) by the designers about what makes a P&C game fun. There are some truly annoying pixel-hunting parts of the game where you are supposed to find incredibly tiny hot-spots to click on, without any clue or evidence on what you're even looking for (I'm looking at you, statue outside of the gate in Chapter 3). There is also a few parts where the game degenerates into "try every combination" territory, where you don't really have a solid puzzle-solving reason to do something, it's just on the list of things you haven't tried yet.
But, honestly, these are common mistakes for early P&C adventures, so for a game like this to be not worth the time, it has to have something else going wrong. And the rest of this game really does well. It has solid puzzles, great ambient sound, and a very interesting murder-mystery-in-castle-full-of-intrigue plot. The only thing in the production values that didn't impress me was the voice acting. It was a little stilted, especially for the protagonist. But it wasn't too distracting from the interesting setting.
It's fun. It's a lot more simplistic and easy and buggy but its a fun game.

Top-notch sound effects, art direction and voice acting conspire to create an amazing atmosphere in this adventure game. The plot is also pretty engaging, even though it gives away its big mysteries too quickly. Fortunately the detective aspect i.e. finding out the secret motivations of all the protagonists is alive and well: along with the great, period-appropriate dialog, it gives me an Agatha Christie novel vibe.
Unfortunately all this goodness comes with pretty serious problems, serious enough that I can't really recommend the game except for dedicated and very patient adventure game fans:
- You can't pick up stuff until the game decides that it makes sense. Sometimes it'll makes sense to you too, i.e. find boards you need to remove and then pick up the hammer you saw somewhere, but at other times it's just a matter of passing a certain point in the story. You could argue this is done in the name of logic, but the game loves to break its own rules from time to time, i.e.
! Your character will also sometimes pick up random stuff with no justification or a lame excuse, which really stands out as wrong given the above emphasis on logic.
- Often NPCs will make something for you, but tell you to wait some time until it's ready. This sometimes means that you need to wander around clicking stuff until the game decides enough time has passed, and at other times that a specific event or dialogue must happen before you can go back. Of course the game won't tell you which, so that leads to a lot of aimless backtracking, and trying to speak again to the same NPC multiple times to check if enough time has passed.
- The above-mentioned backtracking is made way worse by very slow animations when you engage conversations with an NPC. They'll usually calmly finish what they're doing before paying attention to you. To be fair, at first I loved the pacing that created, it does give some dignity to those characters. But they should just have cut those short after the Nth time speaking to an NPC: it eventually just becomes a waste of your time.
- Your character switches occasionally from noble dude to complete jackass. In some instance he seems to question his own behavior which suggests it might be part of the plot, but often it's just stupid adventure game logic, i.e. give someone a fake item just so he'll share details with you.
- One section of the game (
) was basically filler which did almost nothing to advance the plot, and rather detracted from the overall atmosphere.
- I've started encountering instances where you could do something wrong and then if you had the unfortunate idea to save, be stuck in a situation where you're ensured of dying, forcing you to go back to an earlier save or even restart the game (if you, gods forbid, only keep one save).
- The game runs fine on Windows 7 x64, but I'm getting a lot of screen tearing which I haven't found a solution to yet.
All in all I'm almost recommending it because the athmosphere is captivating throughout, and the story is decent almost until the end. However the ending is disappointing and I guessed the solution to the big mystery way before the protagonist realizes it in-game, which made for a tedious, "going through the motions" end-game. Mostly however, this is not a game which respects your time, and after my play sessions I felt disappointed by the time spent/fun had ratio.
You should absolutely play Black Mirror II and III though, they are from a different developer, and absolutely stellar in comparison.

Free to play now, eh?  Well, I got it on sale for a decent discount, so I'm not too ruffled over that.
So, my 0.6 hours of play time should speak volumes about how good I felt this one was.  Yeah, yeah, one should have more play time before posting a review.
It's probably better now than it was when it first came out, but after a few minutes of play that weren't fun, well, I didn't bother spending more time to see if *MAYBE* it got better.  The concept has potential but the execution falls a bit short of the mark.
On the hunting side of things, you basically have one player who puts up a "dome" around the monster so it can't get out.  He doesn't do much else.  This limits the play area.  Big, nicely detailed maps and you get stuck in a tiny circle for many of the fights.  Yeah, I don't like that.  Then the game gets reduced to a small arena where the game defaults to tank, healer, DPS and sort-of crowd control versus Onyxia, or whatever the monster is.
Meh.  That's right.  Meh.  Like fetch quest meh.
I think the game would be alot better if getting hurt meant longer lasting damage, the hunters seem to be able to heal up pretty fast, and it becomes a game of swat the healer first.  I know, all you WOW addicts do that anyway because I did when I played WOW.  Where the heck are the games where the strategy doesn't have to be "gank the healer first"?  I want a game like this one where you can't just point a magic heal-gun at people and... well, heal 'em.
The other down side, for me anyway, is that the monster basically plays hide and seek for a while before it evolves into something that can actually fight a bit.  I think it'd be way more fun if combat was viable right from the start, but with a smaller monster you'd have to use stealthy hit-and-run tactics.  This is pointless because you've got a frickin' heal-bot.
Maybe it'd also be better if you chose the level of evolution at the beginning and the hunters don't know what they're up against untl they finally see the monster.  Each level of evolution could differ in health, speed, stealth, and abilities, but would not necessarily evolve during gameplay because, really, something growing and changing that much, that fast, is silly.
I just feel like it was a bad decision to have the monsters grow and evolve so fast and to let the hunters heal up so easily.  Well, at least when a top level monster isn't knocking their heads together anyway.  I know, I know.  The game's called Evolve.  I get it.
Maybe I'm wrong, but the constantly mixed reviews and small player base at least back up the fact that the game just isn't that great.  Still, tonne of potential.
Still, now that it's free, I recommend that you give it a try.  Maybe you'll like it more than I did.  I will give it thumbs up (thumb... I guess, it's just one) because it's a different concept for multiplayer, and know what you're buying...er... getting for free so . . . buyer bewa... er... free-er beware?  Downloaders beware.  Yes, that's it.  Maybe I'll give it another go someday... when I'm really, really bored.  If I do, and I like it more, I'll change my review.  Enjoy, or not.  :)

I will now review as much of the game as I have experienced so far:
I start the game, the menu is well designed and easy to navigate and pleasant.  The music is good to boot!
Then I press the "New Game" button and prepare myself to create my very first character.  Sitting at the edge of my seat my imagination goes wild with the vast array of possibilities.
Then the best part, the screen goes black and fidgets and the game pops up with a "an error has occured" page and asks if I would like to report it.  Being of sound mind and body, I decide to report it.  The game then restarts and I am free to roam the menus free from errors once again.
In closing I will say that this game is a wonderful addition to the burgeoning Menu Simulator genre.  A genre that I truly hope continues to grow as game developers show love and attention in creating games that function properly.
Note: I will expand this review if and when I get the game to run as advertised.  Furthermore,  I will change this to review to recommend the game if one of two things happens.
1. If the game developer changes the genre to "Fantasy Menu Simulator" and advertises it as such. OR
2. If a patch comes out, making it so that as a consumer I do not need to immediately fix the "finished" product I have purchased and the game is indeed as fun as it looks.
As it sits, based on my experience I cannot recommend this game even if it were free.  Due to the fact that from my current expercience and perspective I would be telling people to install a game that cannot make it past the menu.
Edit: Thanks to a very helpful fan of the game I have found out that the game is indeed free and you may find it at
However, this does not change my opinion.  I cannot recommend spending time trying to get a game to run that has been out since 2012, and has been actively updated and patched since that time (again huge props to the dev for that) but still is difficult to get running on a mid-level gaming PC.  I understand some long standing fans will disagree with me, and that is fine, this is a free country after all.
Final Edit: Clearly the fans of this game are dedicated.  So, if this game can inspire the kind of loyalty I witnessed since writing one long-winded negative review than it must be a good game, because the mob is never wrong. Thank you. Specifically to those who commented on my review for giving me a good chuckle, that has made my time with this game worth while.

ToME is a great true, modern roguelike, and I highly recommend it - above Dungeons of Dredmor and Sword of the Stars: The Pit (the other true roguelikes I own on Steam). The graphics and UI are decent, there's a ton of lore, quests, races & classes, lots of unlockable stuff (including classes), sound+music, etc.
The gameplay is challenging, but there are multiple difficulty levels. ToME uses Diablo-style skill trees and an MMO-style  (i.e. cooldown and resource limited) character abilities system.
ToME also supports user-created addons via either Steam Workshop or the game's web site
, which is great for fixing annoyances and/or adding conveniences as desired.
The game is actively maintained, with regular releases that add new content and features, and rebalance various aspects of the game.
If you like roguelikes and/or ToME looks interesting to you, I strongly suggest trying the demo from their website.

The Typing of The Dead: Overkill has an interesting idea with fairly good execution. The story, while a satire of the tropes found in most zombie flicks, is engaging and had me laughing when films such as Shaun of the Dead didn't get so much as a chuckle out of me. This game has been revamped and the career mode has been redone. The redo, however, is nowhere near where the game used to be, which is saying something. For starters, you can customize your player avatar, but when you're playing the career mode, your character is noticably absent from the screen. There's just a room where you have to click on various items in your room to do different things. You have to manage various needs (energy, rage, hunger, and bladder) while you play. Also, the choice of game (MOBA vs FPS) has been taken away and you're forced into being a FPS gamer, which I didn't want to be. I just played one match and you sit there and are forced to watch 30 rounds of repetitive sounds going back and forth as you're either part of the terrorist or counter-terrorist teams trying to arm or disarm the bomb. I am severely hoping this is merely a phase 1 of the remake and not the whole thing. If this remake is the whole career mode, then I can't believe I'm actually saying that the game took a huge step back.
